title: Jordan's 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
title_zh: 乔丹“最后一舞”球衣拍出创纪录的1060万英镑

image.credit: Photo by Keith Christian Armada on Unsplash
image.author: Keith Christian Armada

lead: A Michael Jordan jersey from his famous 'Last Dance' season has been sold for $14m (£10.6m), setting a new record for basketball memorabilia. The buyer is a Miami real estate investor.
lead_zh: 迈克尔·乔丹在著名的“最后一舞”赛季穿过的一件球衣以1400万美元（约合1060万英镑）售出，创下篮球纪念品的新纪录。买家是迈阿密的一位房地产投资者。
preview: The jersey was worn by Jordan during game two of the 1998 NBA Finals, when he played for the Chicago Bulls, and it also carries his autograp
preview_zh: 这件球衣是乔丹在1998年NBA总决赛第二场比赛中穿过的，当时他效力于芝加哥公牛队，上面还有他的亲笔签名。那晚他拿下了全场最高的37分。随后他以4比2赢下系列赛，结束了在公牛队的最后一个赛季，赢得个人第六个也是最后一个NBA总冠军。在他六次夺冠中，他都当选了总决赛最有价值球员。
paragraphs: The jersey was worn by Jordan during game two of the 1998 NBA Finals, when he played for the Chicago Bulls, and it also carries his autograph. That evening he scored a game-high 37 points. He then ended his final season with the Bulls by winning the series 4-2, claiming his sixth and last NBA Championship. He was named Finals MVP in all six of his championship wins.

The only sports memorabilia item that has ever cost more is the jersey worn by baseball legend Babe Ruth when he 'called the shot' during the 1932 World Series. It was sold for $24.1m (£18.2m) in 2024. Before this sale, the highest price for a basketball item was a 2007-08 card featuring both Jordan and Kobe Bryant, which went for $12.9m (£9.8m) last year.

The previous record for a piece of game-worn Jordan memorabilia had been set just two weeks earlier. His jersey from game three of the 1998 Finals, which is not autographed, was sold at auction for $12.3m (£9.3m). The latest purchase was made by Ron Firman, a Miami real estate investor, in a private sale through Hunt Auctions.

David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, said in a statement that Michael Jordan's importance in the sports memorabilia market had long been established. He added that it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art.
paragraphs_zh: 这件球衣是乔丹在1998年NBA总决赛第二场比赛中穿过的，当时他效力于芝加哥公牛队，上面还有他的亲笔签名。那晚他拿下了全场最高的37分。随后他以4比2赢下系列赛，结束了在公牛队的最后一个赛季，赢得个人第六个也是最后一个NBA总冠军。在他六次夺冠中，他都当选了总决赛最有价值球员。
唯一比它更贵的体育纪念品，是棒球传奇人物贝比·鲁斯在1932年世界大赛中“预言本垒打”时所穿的球衣，它在2024年以2410万美元（约合1820万英镑）售出。在这次交易之前，篮球物品的最高价是一张2007-08赛季乔丹和科比·布莱恩特合体的球星卡，去年以1290万美元（约合980万英镑）成交。
乔丹比赛穿过的纪念品此前的纪录，仅仅在两周前才刚被刷新。他在1998年总决赛第三场穿过的球衣（没有签名）在拍卖会上以1230万美元（约合930万英镑）售出。最新这件球衣由迈阿密房地产投资者罗恩·菲尔曼通过亨特拍卖行私下购得。
亨特拍卖行总裁大卫·亨特在一份声明中表示，迈克尔·乔丹在体育纪念品市场中的重要地位早已确立。他补充说，如今这已经升级为一种精英资产类别，通常只有标志性艺术品才享有这种待遇。

title_original: Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
summary_original: A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season sells for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.
body_original:
Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
By
Ben Collins
BBC Sport journalist
Published
5 hours ago
A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season has sold for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.
Jordan wore the Chicago Bulls jersey during game two of the 1998 NBA Finals and has autographed it too.
He scored a game-high 37 points that evening before ending his last season with the Bulls with a 4-2 series win for his sixth and final NBA Championship. He was named the Finals' Most Valuable Player in all six.
The only item of sports memorabilia that has cost more is the jersey worn by baseball legend Babe Ruth when he "called the shot" during the 1932 World Series, which was sold for $24.1m (£18.2m) in 2024.
The previous high for a basketball item was a card featuring Jordan and Kobe Bryant from 2007-08 which
sold for $12.9m (£9.8m) last year.
The previous record for a piece of game-worn Jordan memorabilia was set just two weeks ago when his jersey from game three of the 1998 Finals, which is not autographed,
sold via auction for $12.3m (£9.3m).
The latest purchase was made by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman in a private sale through Hunt Auctions.
David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, said in a statement: "While Michael Jordan's importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established, it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art."
